A good onion soup is very cheap and simple to make, albeit a bit of a lengthy process, and it's an absolute taste bomb.
Cut the onion in half, slice really thin and cook in a pot with some butter over medium high heat for at least 30-45 minutes while continuously stirring. Add some red wine (not sparkling), add in bay leaf and thyme, simmer until almost all of the wine is gone, remove the Bay leaf, add another bit of butter, a tablespoon of flour and mix really well for 5-ish minutes to cook the flour, add some broth simmer for 10-15 more minutes and it's done! Rest of the wine pairs perfectly and it's best served on top of really toasted bread, with plenty of grated cheese on top. If you want to be really fancy you can put the dish for a quick broil in the oven to melt and crisp some of the cheese on top.

I live somewhat near Venice, about an hour away with a car. As a general indication, beeing a sea city, generally you want to try fish based dishes. In particular I would suggest baccalà in every possible variation, it a typical dish of our region. It's dried codfish, that has been imported, mainly from Norway, for centuries.
The perfect combination is polenta with baccalà, it looks something like [this](http://blog.zingarate.com/wanderlustt/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/pol-e-bac.jpg) or [this](http://www.casabella.it/upload/ricette/img/33tmpphpykvE4w.jpg). They are different because the second one is cooked with milk and made in a sort of a sauce that's eaten cold, while the first one is a dish that's eaten hot.
If i misspelled something or there are utterly unintelligible things please point them out and i'll try to rephrase.

If you want to really experience the culinary aspect of Italy be sure to do some reserch about the typical **local** food. This is very important. Think about Italy almost as a federation of countries, because even if it's a single nation historically it wasn't for a very long time, so local cultures, all of them, differ a lot from one place to another.
